A 75year-old female patient with fever and cough showed positive for nucleic acid antibodies.
First chest CT (Fig.1 A1A3) showed novel coronavirus pneumonia (COVID-19) and bilateral adrenal glands were normal.
Due to left abdomen pain after 2 weeks, chest CT and abdominal CT enhanced scan showed expanded infection in bilateral lungs and bilateral adrenal hemorrhages (AH)
(Fig.1 B1B3, Fig. 2).

Laboratory tests: plasma Ddimers elevated (3.11 mg/L), monocyte count elevated (4.27×109/L), norepinephrine increased 6.38 μmol/24 hours, serum ACTH increased (73pg/ml), serum cortisol and serum sodium decreased (98nmol/L, 123mmol/L, respectively).
Blood pressure was 100/60mmHg.
After 2 weeks chest and abdominal CT (Fig. 1 C1C3) indicated infection reduce in bilateral lungs.
Adrenal hemorrhage reduced in right side and increased in left side.
COVID-19 was treated with hormones (methylprednisolone, qd 40 mg, 5 days).

After hormonal, anticoagulant, hemostatic and antiviral treatment, the patient was discharged from the hospital.
Reexamination showed bilateral adrenal hemorrhages reduced after 2 months (Fig.1 D1D3).
Is a AH caused by COVID-19 rare extrapulmonary complication (1) and can lead to acute adrenal insufficiency and even death.

Currently, the pathogenesis of AH may be: (i) vascular rupture bleeding due to the increased adrenal vein pressure (2), (ii) vascular rupture caused by adrenal vascular endothelial cell injury (3), (iii) immune response that destroys adrenal tissue (4).
Neurological manifestations of COVID-19 do also innitiate this workup (5).
It was always neglected because the atypical symptoms of AH in clinic.
